newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF BENFICA V PORTO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF BENFICA V PORTO.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Benfica and Porto who meet in the Portuguese first division championship on Saturday (2130 GMT):

Playing style - Brazilian coach Paulo Autuori has experimented with both 4-4-2 and 4-3-3 without fixing on a definite style. Unlike Porto, who prefer to counter-punch, Benfica like to attack from the start, relying on a creative midfield.
Strengths - A talented midfield, with veteran Brazilian Valdo Filho masterminding the moves, and the attacking flair of its captain Joao Vieira Pinto.

Weakness - The failure to develop a clear style of play with the result the team is dependent on individual moments of brilliance. The defence tends to be static, lacking players who like to push forward down the flanks.

Motivation - Defeat for Benfica on Saturday would virtually hand the championship to their bitter rivals. Porto already hold a five point lead at the top of the table. Last season the home side won 2-1, ending an unbeaten Porto run of over 50 games, and Benfica would love to do it again.

Playing style - Coach Antonio Oliveira is expected to adopt a 4-3-3 line up, but with three central defenders in the backline, as he has done in all the club's most difficult games this season. Porto will leave the home side to take the initiative.

Strengths - Porto have probably the greatest depth of talent in the Portuguese league. The defence, with tough-tackling Jorge Costa at its heart, is hard to penetrate. Its strike force is so complete that top-scoring Mario Jardel often begins on the bench.

Weaknesses - No real weak spots. The club could have faced a problem in goal after the transfer of Vitor Baia to Barcelona at the end of last season but Henrique Hilario, getting his first taste of top level soccer, has proved a worthy replacement.
Motivation - After winning back-to-back league titles, champions Porto could make it a record third. Motivation is not lacking particularly against traditional rivals Benfica.
